title: Ignacio Meyer Named President of Universal Music Latin America & Iberian Peninsula
summary: He will report to Felipe Holguín, who was named CEO of the division this week.
contentText:
Ignacio Meyer has been named president of Universal Music Latin America & Iberian Peninsula, effective immediately, Billboard can announce Wednesday (Nov. 18). He will report to Felipe Holguín , who was named CEO of the division on Tuesday (Nov. 17) after it was announced Monday (Nov. 16) that Jesús López was stepping down from the position.

“Artists are at the heart of how we’re building this next chapter. Nacho combines creative sensibility and strategic vision with a deep understanding of how to nurture each artist’s individuality, grow their audience, and heighten their impact across platforms,” Holguín said in a press statement. “He’ll add a powerful dimension to our leadership team as we invest in extraordinary artists and bring bold ideas to life. We know from experience how well we work together, and I’m delighted to welcome him to UMG.”

Prior to joining the Universal Music team, Meyer — a 2026 Billboard Latin Power Player — was president of Univision Networks Group and previously held leadership roles at TelevisaUnivision since 2011, spanning U.S. networks and local media, radio, music and non-scripted entertainment, business development and strategic partnerships. In early October, Billboard announced that Meyer was stepping down from his post at TelevisaUnivision.

“Latin music is shaping culture around the world because its artists keep pushing boundaries by embracing new sounds, new technologies, and new ways to connect with fans,” added Meyer. “Their creative ambition is a force for the entire industry. Our role is to amplify that vision with the right support, fresh thinking, and UMG’s global reach. I’m excited to work with Felipe and our teams to help artists build lasting careers and take their music even further.”

Meyer is the first senior appointment by Holguín, who was recently named CEO of Universal Music Latin America & Iberian Peninsula and will be based in Miami, reporting directly to Sir Lucian Grainge , chairman and CEO of UMG.
